primary_claim: Applying METR's task-horizon methodology to offensive cybersecurity, frontier LLMs' 50%-success task horizon on cyber tasks is doubling roughly every 5 months, and the best current models solve only 6-minute tasks at 50% success, about a tenth of METR's software-engineering horizon.

effect.value: ~5 months; best models reach a 6-minute P(50) horizon (exponential fit R²=0.94)

contradicts_or_qualifies: The cyber task horizon (~6 minutes) is about a tenth of the ~60-minute horizon METR found for software-engineering tasks, while doubling somewhat faster (~5 months vs METR's ~7 months)
stated_future_work: Extending this methodology to scheming-capability horizons
limitations_stated: Human task time lengths are mostly AI-assisted estimates rather than genuine human baselines
Near-certain dataset contamination, since many tasks were likely included in model pretraining sets
Prompt, few-shot template, and tool-call budget design choices could systematically inflate or depress scores
Each model attempted every task only once, so stochastic variance in outputs could shift success rates
Automatic LLM-based functional-equivalence grading may occasionally misjudge success or failure
quote: Cyber task horizons are doubling every ~5 months.
